Chapter 6: The Practice of Persistent Prayer—Staying Faithful Over Time
So, let’s talk about what it really means to stick with prayer for the long haul—especially as a parent. You know, once you’ve learned to trust and surrender, the next big step is all about persistence. Think of parenting as this winding journey, where sometimes you’re just waiting, not sure what’s coming next, or wondering if anything’s even changing.
The idea here is to see prayer not as a one-and-done thing, but as something you keep coming back to. Imagine tending a garden: some days, it feels like nothing’s happening, but you still water, you still care, and eventually, you notice growth. Persistent prayer works the same way.
It’s really about showing up, over and over, no matter what’s going on or how things look on the surface. Maybe you’re bringing the same worries, hopes, or dreams to God day after day. Even if you don’t see instant results, every single prayer matters. It’s not about trying to convince or pester the divine—far from it. It’s about showing that you’re committed, that you’re faithful.
Now, how do you make this work in real life? Here are a few gentle practices that can help:
First, try setting rhythms and reminders. Maybe you pick a time each day—like during your morning walk, at bedtime, or even while you’re driving—to pause and pray. Little cues, like a photo of your child or a sticky note on the fridge, can help you remember to lift them up in prayer.
Another helpful habit is keeping a prayer journal. Write down your specific hopes, concerns, and even the answers you see along the way. This can be so encouraging, especially when you notice a prayer has been answered or some small sign of progress appears that you might’ve missed otherwise.
And don’t worry about repeating yourself. Bringing the same concern to God again and again isn’t a sign of weak faith—it’s more like watering a seed. Each prayer nurtures hope and trust, even when change feels slow.
Picture a parent whose child is facing a long-term challenge—like a learning disability or a tough friendship. The progress might be slow, and there will be days when setbacks hit hard. In these moments, persistent prayer helps you stay engaged, hopeful, and present, even if you can’t fix things right away.
Here’s what’s really comforting: being faithful in prayer is itself a powerful act of love. Every prayer—no matter how quick or simple—adds another thread to your child’s story. Over time, these threads come together to create a legacy of care, faith, and resilience.
